questions.question: Read PR #201 and compare its proposal with the indexed implementation of _aget_relevant_documents. Is the proposed concurrency already present in this snapshot?

alternatives.excerpt:
async def _aget_relevant_documents(
        self,
        query: str,
        *,
        run_manager: AsyncCallbackManagerForRetrieverRun,
    ) -> list[Document]:
        del run_manager
        vector_rows, keyword_rows = await asyncio.gather(
            self._vector_candidates(query),
            self._keyword_candidates(query),
        )
        fused = self._fuse_candidates(vector_rows, keyword_rows)
        return await self._parent_documents(fused[: self.final_k * 3])

reference_facts.text: PR #201 proposes concurrent semantic and keyword retrieval on one connection.
The frozen implementation calls both candidate methods through asyncio.gather.
That concurrency is already present in the indexed snapshot; the proposal alone does not demonstrate a new behavior or merged improvement.

reference_facts.text: PR #202 proposes transactional index replacement and claims previous-index chat stays available after a failed reindex.
Promotion already performs replacement and READY update inside a transaction; a failed transaction can preserve the previous rows.
The worker marks the repository FAILED on indexing errors, while chat requires READY.
Therefore preserved old rows do not establish chat availability: the pinned code blocks chat after FAILED, contrary to that part of the PR claim.
